Rashi on Eruvin 91a:12:1.hebrew: היינו דמשכחת לה מאני דבתים בחצר - דאיצטריך למיתני: "אבל לא לכלים ששבתו בתוך הבית":
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:12:1.english: That is how you find vessels of the houses in the courtyard - Such that it was necessary to teach: "But not for vessels that rested inside the house."

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:13:1.hebrew: בכומתא וסודרא - ששבתו בתוך הבית, והוציאן לחצר דרך מלבוש:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:13:1.english: With a cap and a scarf - Which rested inside the house, and he brought them out into the courtyard by way of clothing [i.e., by wearing them].

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:1:1.hebrew: וקרפיפות רשות לעצמן - ואפילו הן של ב' אנשים, מטלטלין מזה לזה. דהאמר ר"מ: "כל גגות העיר רשות אחת", שמע מינה דס"ל דאין רשות מתחלקת מחמת שינוי בעלים, אלא בתים לחודייהו, מפני שהם תדירות לדירה — דמה לי גגין, ומה לי חצירות, ומה לי קרפיפות. אבל מגג לחצר ומגג לקרפף, לר"מ לא, ואפילו של איש אחד — כדאמרינן: גזירה משום תל ברה"ר, וכ"ש כשהן של שנים. ומחצר לקרפף נמי לא, דשמעינן להו לרבנן לקמן בברייתא דאסור לטלטל מחצר לקרפף, ור"מ לא שמעינן ליה דפליג עלייהו להקל אלא בחלוק רשויות דגגין, הואיל ושמן שוה. אבל ברשויות החלוקות בשמן לא שמעינן ליה דמיקל, דדוקא קאמר ר"מ גגות, דתשמישתן שוה, וכן חצירות, וכן קרפיפות, ואפילו הן של שנים — דבשינוי בעלים לא מיתסרי אלא בתים לר"מ וגגין לרבנן, אבל בחלוק תשמיש ושינוי שם הרשות קפיד. הלכך, מחצר לקרפף אסור, ואפילו הוא שלו ואינו יותר מבית סאתים — דעל כרחך הנך קרפיפות בשאין יתירים על בית סאתים קאמר, דאי ביתירים, בהא לימא רבי שמעון מטלטלין?! הא כרמלית היא, וליכא מאן דפליג, דמחצר המשכן גמרי! ועוד, בהדיא אמרינן בשלהי עושין פסין דפלוגתא דר"ש ורבנן בקרפף בית סאתים היא, ואפילו חצר וקרפף של איש אחד אסרי רבנן; דקאמרי התם: "קרפף יותר מבית סאתים שהוקף לדירה, נזרע רובו — הרי הוא כגנה כו'", ואמר רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע כו', וכי דייקת בה שמעינן מינה דלא שרי ר"ש אלא בקרפף בית סאתים, ורבנן אסרי אע"ג דלחד גברא הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:1:1.english: And enclosures are a domain in and of themselves - And even if they belong to two people, one may carry from this one to that one. For since Rabbi Meir said: "All the roofs of the city are one domain," learn from this that he holds that a domain is not divided on account of a change of owners, except for houses alone, because they are regularly [used] for dwelling; for what difference does it make to me [whether they are] roofs, and what difference does it make to me [whether they are] courtyards, and what difference does it make to me [whether they are] enclosures? However, [carrying] from a roof to a courtyard and from a roof to an enclosure, according to Rabbi Meir, is not [permitted], even [if both belong] to one person, as we say: [It is a rabbinic] decree on account of a mound in a public domain; and all the more so when they belong to two [people]. And from a courtyard to an enclosure, too, [carrying is] not [permitted], for we hear the Rabbis later in a baraita [stating] that it is prohibited to carry from a courtyard to an enclosure, and we do not hear that Rabbi Meir disputes them to be lenient except regarding the division of domains of roofs, since their name is identical; but regarding domains that are divided in their name, we do not hear that he is lenient. For Rabbi Meir specifically said [this regarding] roofs, whose usage is identical, and likewise courtyards, and likewise enclosures, and even if they belong to two [people] — for on account of a change of owners, [carrying] is not prohibited except [between] houses according to Rabbi Meir, and [between] roofs according to the Rabbis; but [Rabbi Meir] is strict regarding a difference in usage and a change in the name of the domain. Therefore, [carrying] from a courtyard to an enclosure is prohibited, and even [if] it is his [own] and [the enclosure] is not more than two beit se'ah. For perforce, [when Rav Yehuda mentioned] these enclosures, he was speaking [only] when they do not exceed two beit se'ah; for if [they were] exceeding [two beit se'ah], in such a case would Rabbi Shimon say that one may carry?! Behold, it is a karmelit, and there is no one who disputes [this], as they derive [it] from the courtyard of the Tabernacle! And furthermore, we explicitly say at the end of [the chapter entitled] "Osin Passin" that the dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis is regarding an enclosure of two beit se'ah, and even [in the case of] a courtyard and an enclosure of one person, the Rabbis prohibit [carrying between them]; as they say there: "An enclosure greater than two beit se'ah that was enclosed for dwelling, [and] the majority of it was sown, behold it is like a garden...", etc., and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said..., etc., and when you examine it closely, we learn from it that Rabbi Shimon permits only in [the case of] an enclosure of two beit se'ah, and the Rabbis prohibit, even though it belongs to one person.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:1:2.hebrew: לדברי חכמים - דלא גזרו משום תל — גגין וחצירות רשות אחת הן. לא שיטלטל מגג לגג אם חלוקין בעליהן, משום דגגין לרבנן כבתים משוי להן על ידי חילוק שלמטה; אבל מחצר של רבים לחצר של רבים מטלטלין, ומגג לחצר דרבים מטלטלין. ואע"ג דגג רשותא דידיה וחצר דשותפות, כדתניא בברייתא לקמן — הואיל וגג תשמיש שאינו תדיר הוא, לא הוי ממש כבית, ומטלטל ממנו לחצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:1:2.english: According to the statement of the Sages - Who did not issue a decree due to [the concern of] a mound — roofs and courtyards are one domain. Not that one may carry from roof to roof if their owners are divided, because according to the Rabbis, they treat roofs like houses by virtue of the division below; rather, from a courtyard belonging to many to a courtyard belonging to many one may carry, and from a roof to a courtyard belonging to many one may carry. And even though the roof is his own [private] domain and the courtyard is jointly owned, as is taught in the baraita below — since a roof is [put to] infrequent use, it is not truly like a house, and [one may] carry from it to the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:1:3.hebrew: קרפיפות רשות אחת - ואפילו הן של שנים, דכל רשות ששמו שוה מותר לו, חוץ מן הגגין. אבל מחצר לקרפף, אפילו דחד גברא — אסיר, ולא דמי לגג וחצר, דתשמישתיה דגג שוה לחצר הוא. והכי שמיע ליה לרב יהודה, וממתניתין דייק לה: מדקאמר ר"ש "כולן רשות אחת", מכלל דרבנן לאו חדא רשותא משוי להו לכולהו. וברייתא מסייעא ליה לקמן, דקתני: גג וחצר ואכסדרה ומרפסת כולן רשות אחת הן, וחצר ומרפסת כב' חצירות דמי. ומדוקיא דידה, דלא תנא בה קרפף ומבוי, מוקמינן לה כרבנן; דאי ר"ש, אפילו קרפף נמי מישתרי בהדי חצר, ואי ר"מ, גג וחצר לא מישתרו, דהא בהדיא אסר במתני' מנמוך לגבוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:1:3.english: Enclosures are one domain - And even if they belong to two [different people], for [carrying within] any domain whose designation is the same is permitted to one, except for roofs. But [carrying] from a courtyard to an enclosure, even [if both belong] to one person, is prohibited; and it is not comparable to a roof and a courtyard, for the usage of a roof is similar to [that of] a courtyard. And this is how Rav Yehuda received it, and from our Mishnah he deduces it: from [the fact] that Rabbi Shimon says, “All of them are one domain,” by inference the Rabbis do not make all of them into a single domain. And a baraita later supports him, as it teaches: “A roof, a courtyard, a portico, and a balcony are all one domain, and a courtyard and a balcony are considered like two courtyards.” And from an inference of its [wording], since it did not teach an enclosure or an alleyway in it, we establish it in accordance with the Rabbis; for if [it were in accordance with] Rabbi Shimon, even an enclosure would also be permitted together with a courtyard; and if [it were in accordance with] Rabbi Meir, a roof and a courtyard would not be permitted, for he explicitly prohibited in the Mishnah [carrying] from a low [domain] to an elevated [domain].

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:1.hebrew: לדברי ר"ש כולן רשות אחת - דלא תימא: האי דא"ר שמעון אחד גגות ואחד חצירות ואחד קרפיפות, כל חדא וחדא רשותא באנפי נפשיה משוי לה — גגין לעצמן, וחצירות לעצמן, וקרפיפות לעצמן, דהא סברא לר"מ אית ליה; אבל ר"ש כולהו חדא רשותא משוי להו. הכי שמיע ליה לרב יהודה, וברייתא מסייעא ליה, דתניא כוותיה לקמן: היינו מעלין שמן ואלונטית מגג לגג, ומגג לחצר, ומחצר לחצר, ומחצר לקרפף:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:1.english: According to the statement of Rabbi Shimon, all of them are one domain - Lest you say that this which Rabbi Shimon said, "Whether roofs, or courtyards, or enclosures," [means that] he renders each and every one a domain unto itself — roofs by themselves, courtyards by themselves, and enclosures by themselves — for this reasoning belongs to Rabbi Meir; but Rabbi Shimon renders all of them one [single] domain. This is how Rav Yehuda understood it, and a baraita supports him, as it is taught in accordance with his view below: "We would carry oil and a towel from roof to roof, and from roof to courtyard, and from courtyard to courtyard, and from courtyard to an enclosure."

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:2.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב - דאמר לעיל (עירובין פט.) בגגין השוין לרבנן, דאין מטלטלין בו אלא בד', דאסרי אהדדי, ולא אמרינן גוד אסיק במחיצות שאין ניכרות:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:2.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav - For he said above (Eruvin 89a) regarding level roofs, according to the Rabbis, that one may carry on [each roof] only within four [cubits], for they prohibit one another, and we do not say "extend and raise" in the case of partitions that are not recognizable.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:3.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב יהודה - אליבא דר"ש:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:3.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda - According to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:4.hebrew: ואסור להעלות ולהוריד - ר"מ לטעמיה, דגזר משום תל:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:4.english: And it is prohibited to carry up and carry down - Rabbi Meir [follows] his reasoning, as he decrees on account of a mound:

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:5.hebrew: מותר לטלטלן בחצר - אע"פ שלא עירבה, וה"ה לשאר חצירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:5.english: It is permitted to carry them in the courtyard - Even though [its residents] did not make an eiruv; and the same applies to other courtyards:

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:6.hebrew: רשות לעצמו - ואין מטלטלין מזה לזה, אפילו תוך ד':
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:6.english: A domain in and of itself - And one may not carry from this [roof] to that [roof], even within four [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:2:7.english: And one may not carry on it - Even on the roof itself.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:3:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרב יהודה - אליבא דר"ש:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:3:1.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda - According to [the view of] Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:3:3.english: A towel - To dry oneself with it:

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:3:4.english: From roof to roof, and from roof to courtyard, and from courtyard to enclosure, and from enclosure to enclosure - We read all of them [in the text].

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:7:1.hebrew: והוא שלא עירבו - בני החצירות, כל אחת לעצמה. דהשתא לא שכיחי כלי הבתים בחצר, וליכא למיגזר: אי שרית להוציא כלים ששבתו בזו להכניסן לחברתה, אתי לאפוקי נמי כלי הבית:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:7:1.english: Provided that they did not establish an eiruv - [Namely,] the residents of the courtyards, each one for itself. For now, vessels of the houses are not commonly found in the courtyard, and there is no [reason] to decree: If you permit taking out vessels that rested in this [courtyard] to bring them into its neighboring [courtyard], one will come to take out vessels of the house as well.

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:7:2.hebrew: אבל עירבו - כל חצר לעצמה, ולא עירבו שתי החצירות יחד — אסור לטלטל מזו לזו, אפילו כלי החצר; דכיון דשכיחי מאני דבתים בחצר, גזרינן דילמא אתי לאפוקי מאני דבתים שבחצר זו לחצר זו. ור"ש מודה בהו, דקתני: אבל לא לכלים ששבתו בתוך הבית:
Rashi on Eruvin 91a:7:2.english: However, if they established an eiruv - Each courtyard for itself, and the two courtyards did not establish an eiruv together — it is prohibited to carry from this [courtyard] to that [one], even vessels of the courtyard; for since vessels of the houses are commonly found in the courtyard, we decree lest one come to carry out vessels of the houses that are in this courtyard to that [other] courtyard. And Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding them, as it teaches: “However, not for vessels that rested inside the house.”

Rashi on Eruvin 91a:8:1.english: Who whispered to you - We do not read [this].

Tosafot on Eruvin 91a:7:1.hebrew: אמר רב הלכה כר"ש והוא שלא עירבו - אין לפרש דר"ש אין מחלק בין עירבו ולא עירבו, ורב בלא עירבו סבר ליה כוותיה; דא"כ, בסמוך דפריך רב חסדא לשמואל ור' יוחנן: "יאמרו ב' כלים בחצר אחת זה אסור וזה מותר?", לרב נמי תיקשי אליבא דר"ש! ורב ששת נמי דפריך לרב: "אלא אי אמרת בשלא עירבו היכי משכחת מאני דבתים בחצר?" — הא רב נמי מודה דר"ש אפילו בעירבו קאמר?! ולכך נראה, דרב סבר: דר"ש גופיה לא אמר אלא כשלא עירבו. והשתא סברת שמואל איפכא מדרב: דשמואל לא גזר הכא — דאמר "בין עירבו בין לא עירבו", וגבי שלש חצירות גזר — דסבר כרבנן דאמרי שלשתן אסורות, לשיטת ר"ת דמי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין מח: ד"ה רשות); ורב הכא גזר, והתם לא גזר — דפסיק התם כר"ש. ועוד, דמשני הכא שמואל: "דר"ש לטעמיה דלא גזר", משמע דסבר כוותיה בההיא דג' חצירות, ולשיטת ר"ת סבר כרבנן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 91a:7:1.english: Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, provided that they did not establish an eiruv - One cannot explain that Rabbi Shimon does not distinguish between [whether] they established an eiruv and [whether] they did not establish an eiruv, and Rav holds like him [only] when they did not establish an eiruv; for if so, nearby, where Rav Ḥisda challenges Shmuel and Rabbi Yoḥanan: "[People] will say: Two vessels in one courtyard — this [one] is forbidden and that [one] is permitted?!", [this] should also be difficult for Rav according to the view of Rabbi Shimon! And also Rav Sheshet, who challenges Rav: "Rather, if you say [that it is] when they did not establish an eiruv, how do you find vessels of houses in the courtyard?" — surely Rav also concedes that Rabbi Shimon spoke even when they established an eiruv?! And therefore it appears that Rav holds: Rabbi Shimon himself did not state [his ruling] except when they did not establish an eiruv. And now, Shmuel's reasoning is the reverse of Rav's: for Shmuel did not issue a decree here — as he said "whether they established an eiruv or whether they did not establish an eiruv" — and regarding three courtyards he issued a decree — as he holds in accordance with the Rabbis who say that all three of them are forbidden, according to the approach of Rabbeinu Tam in [the chapter] Mi SheHotzi'uhu (above, Eruvin 48b, s.v. Reshut); and Rav issued a decree here, and there he did not issue a decree — as he ruled there in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. And furthermore, that which [the Gemara] answers here [for] Shmuel: "Rabbi Shimon conforms to his reasoning that he did not issue a decree," implies that he holds like him in that [case] of three courtyards, whereas according to the approach of Rabbeinu Tam, he holds like the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Eruvin 91a:8:1.hebrew: ושמואל אומר בין עירבו בין לא עירבו - והא דאמר שמואל בגיטין בהזורק (דף עט:): "לא יעמוד אדם בגג זה ויקלוט מי גשמים בגגו של חבירו" — אומר ר"י: דהתם לקלוט ולהוליך לביתו קאמר; דכמו שאסור לטלטל כלים ששבתו בבית לחצר ולגג שלא עירבו, אפילו לר"ש, כן אסור מגג וחצר לבית. ודווקא מגגו של חבירו, אבל מגג של עצמו יכול לקלוט ולהוליך לביתו, ואין גג של חבירו אוסר עליו, דשמואל לטעמיה, דאמר לעיל: "גוד אסיק מחיצתא". וא"ת: מאי קמ"ל שמואל? דפשיטא דאסור להוליך לביתו! וי"ל: דאשמעינן דאע"פ שקולט מן האויר, ועדיין לא נגעו מי גשמים בגג:
Tosafot on Eruvin 91a:8:1.english: "And Shmuel says: Whether they established an eiruv or whether they did not establish an eiruv" - And as for that which Shmuel said in Gittin in [the chapter entitled] HaZorek (79b): "A person may not stand on this roof and catch rainwater on the roof of his fellow" — Ri says that there, it means to catch [the water] and bring [it] into his house; for just as it is forbidden to carry utensils that rested in a house into a courtyard or onto a roof when they did not establish an eiruv, even according to Rabbi Shimon, so too is it forbidden [to carry] from a roof or courtyard into a house. And specifically [is this so] from the roof of his fellow; but from his own roof he may catch [water] and bring [it] into his house, and his fellow's roof does not restrict him, for Shmuel is consistent with his own reasoning, as he said earlier: "Extend and project the wall upward." And if you say: What is Shmuel teaching us? For it is obvious that it is forbidden to bring [it] into his house! And one can say: He teaches us that even though he catches [the water] from the air and the rainwater has not yet touched the roof [it is nonetheless forbidden].

Tosafot on Eruvin 91a:8:2.hebrew: מי לחשך - רש"י לא גרס ליה. ואור"י דאיתא בתורת כהנים בכמה מקומות. ור"ת נמי גרס ליה, ומפרש: "מי השמיעך הלכה כר"ש, בין עירבו ובין לא עירבו?". ורבינו שמואל פירש דקאי ארב — כלומר: מי הגיד לך שאתה מחלק ביניהם? אינו כן, אלא בין עירבו ובין לא עירבו. ואית דגרסי "מלחשך" בתיבה אחת, ומפרשי: שנולד מלחש [כדאיתא ביומא פב:]:
Tosafot on Eruvin 91a:8:2.english: "Who whispered to you" - Rashi did not have this reading. And the Ri says that it is found in Torat Kohanim in several places. And Rabbeinu Tam also had this reading, and explains: "Who made you hear [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, whether they established an eiruv or whether they did not establish an eiruv?" And Rabbeinu Shmuel explained that it refers to [the statement of] Rav, as if to say: "Who told you that you should differentiate between them? It is not so; rather, [it is] whether they established an eiruv or whether they did not establish an eiruv." And some read "milchashakh" as a single word, and explain that [it means] he was born from a whisper [as it is found in Yoma 82b].
